characters.name: Tess Vance
characters.goal: clear herself of spoiling the barrels

characters.name: Bruno Callow
characters.goal: blame cellar handling for the spoiled barrels

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the catastrophic ruin of the vintage and shifts suspicion from cellar mismanagement to deliberate tampering.

char_tess.goal: clear herself of spoiling the barrels
prove the topping carboy was tampered with

required_beats: Bruno pulls bungs from three barrels, discovers volatile acetic acid taint across every cask, and accuses Tess of ruining the lots during topping-up.
Tess inspects the topping carboy bung and notices a sweet aroma instead of sanitizing sulphur.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reveals that the topping supply was contaminated with unpasteurized pressings, framing Bruno's actions as desperate corner-cutting.

char_clara.goal: confront Bruno about taking her press wine

required_beats: In the press shed, Tess finds the metabisulphite dispenser locked inside Clara's cabinet.
Clara discovers her experimental tank of unpasteurized pressings was emptied into the carboys and assumes Bruno stole them to stretch volume after the crop loss.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Deepens the mystery as Bruno readily accepts Clara's charge of incompetence to deflect deeper inquiry.
required_beats: In the barrel cellar, Clara confronts Bruno for topping fine wine with raw, unstabilized pressings to mask hailstorm losses.
Bruno accepts the blame for poor cellar judgment while insisting Tess should have spotted the bacterial film, appearing oddly relieved by the accusation.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Exposes Bruno's deliberate sabotage of the vintage and resolves Tess's loyalty through self-preservation.

char_tess.goal: prove the topping carboy was tampered with
force Bruno to sign her wage release in exchange for silence

required_beats: Tess discovers the developer contract stipulating mortgage assumption only if winemaking terminates this winter.
Bruno admits he intentionally used Clara's sour press wash to ruin the stock so Clara would abandon the vineyard.
Tess leverages the contract to demand her full seasonal wages and a written discharge.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Exposes Bruno's deliberate sabotage of the harvest to Clara as Tess quietly secures her severance and departs.

char_tess.goal: force Bruno to sign her wage release in exchange for silence

required_beats: In front of the sour barrels, Bruno hands Tess her final endorsed paycheck and reference letter, remarking callously that Clara was destined to lose the estate anyway.
While Clara frantically tests the sour casks, Tess quietly slips the developer contract out of her coat and leaves it face-up on the tasting table beside Clara's testing kit.
Clara finds the contract on the table and realizes her brother intentionally poisoned her harvest.
Tess leaves the cellar with her money, leaving Clara and Bruno standing amidst the ruined wine in bitter silence.

voice_card.narrative_distance: close third, locked to the viewpoint character; knows only what they know
voice_card.register: alert, concrete, quietly tense; lets a detail sit wrong before explaining it
voice_card.sentence_rhythm: lean sentences that tighten as pressure builds; a short line to land each discovery
voice_card.dialogue_density: moderate to high; people talk around what they are hiding
voice_card.reader_familiarity: The first time a deep term appears (domain-specific jargon), let dialogue or narration make its meaning clear within a clause. Never lecture.

metadata.title: The Acetous Vintage
metadata.source: segmented from a Fabula-only package by gemini-3.8-flash

facts.statement: An early winter hailstorm destroyed fifty percent of the hillside vineyard's fruit yield.
A commercial resort developer offered to pay off all estate debt on the condition that winemaking ceases permanently.
Bruno intentionally filled the glass carboy with active vinegar mother from Clara's pressings to ruin the wine.
Tess performed the routine topping-up of all twelve oak barrels on Tuesday afternoon.
Tess's seasonal employment agreement docks wages and forfeits industry references if spoilage is ruled worker error.
Bruno carries personal liability for the estate's bank loan notes.
The cellar's potassium metabisulphite dosing unit remained locked inside Clara's cabinet throughout the week.
The bung on the topping carboy smelled of unpreserved dessert pressings rather than sulphited cellar wine.
Clara's separate tank containing unpasteurized dessert pressings was emptied into the topping vessels without authorization.
All twelve oak barrels across separate lots succumbed simultaneously to an acute acetic acid bloom.
Clara believed Bruno ruined the vintage through incompetent volume-stretching rather than calculated sabotage.

premise.logline: A vineyard’s whole vintage turns in the barrel, and the cellar hand who topped it up has to work out what went in.

modules.theme: how a family decides which member is expendable
modules.setting_time: the winter after a hailstorm took half the crop
modules.setting_place: a hillside winery run by three siblings who share one cellar
modules.protagonist: a seasonal cellar hand who is not family
modules.protagonist_want: to keep her job by proving the spoilage was not her mistake
modules.antagonism: a sibling who would rather lose the vintage than the argument
modules.complication: the barrels were spoiled to force a sale she would have wanted
modules.ending_shape: the truth comes out, and nobody is better off for it

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.
